summary.headline: Crizac Q2 FY27 operating income fell 36.7% YoY to INR 1,027 million; management guides FY27 revenue and profit in line with FY26 on deferred students.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by the West Asia conflict, currency moves in a key source market, and post-grad students deferring intakes. Operating income was INR 1,027 million (down 36.7% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 330 million (down 44%), and PAT INR 369 million (down 23.7%). Management attributes the shortfall to timing, saying revenue is deferred rather than lost, with Q3 FY27 revenue guided up 10-12% YoY and FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26. An interim dividend of INR 4 per share was declared, and the company reported net cash of about INR 5,984 million.

segments.name: UK (anchor market)
segments.commentary: Management says UK-sponsored study visas fell 20% between FY24 and FY26 while Crizac students grew 53%. Three universities accounted for 44% of revenue. The UK budget of 28 October proposed a 2-year graduate visa for high-compliance universities versus 18 months for others from January 2027; qualifying universities are yet to be defined.

segments.name: Non-UK destinations
segments.commentary: Non-UK destinations were about 9.5% of H1 applications versus 4.7% in H1 FY26, but contributed only 1.4% of revenue as of today. Management targets 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 revenue expected to grow 10-12% YoY over Q3 FY26, based on students who already have admission and visa in place.
FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26, barring any black swan event; management says a large share of Q4 applications is already received and being processed.
Interim dividend INR 4 per share declared; total FY27 dividend including final expected at INR 8-10 per share.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 25-26%, same as last year; salary cost expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term.
No FY28 guidance yet; management says it will be in a better position to guide next quarter. FY28 is subject to market reaction and US mid-term election outcomes.
Acquisitions: targets EBITDA-accretive deals with a 10-20% return, depending on geography; M&A pipeline described as active but cautious.
capex_capacity: Over 600 institutional partners; relationships with the top 30 partners exceed 5 years.
Counselling partner network of more than 18,500, of which 4,942 were active in H1.
Platform processed over 2 lakh applications from 92 countries; enrolment rate 12.8% on a rolling 12-month basis.
USD 2.5 million committed in March 2026 to in-house development of EduMentor, an AI-led student-university matching and mentorship platform.
Asset-light model: accommodation and student loans are distributed as a DSA for third parties; no real estate acquisition planned.
Medway Education (New Zealand) acquired at the start of FY27; New Zealand main intake is February, so revenue lands in Q4.
demand_pricing: Applications fell about 3% YoY in Q2, but revenue fell about 37%. Management attributes the gap to deferral timing, not lower revenue per student or mix.
Market share rose from 3.5% to 6% globally (FY24 to FY26). Share of Indian students rose from 9% to 13.9%, while visas to Indian students fell 22% over the same period.
Share of ex-India students rose from 1.5% to 3.7%.
Students deferred to the November and January intakes. Management says the Q2 shortfall should be recovered in Q3 and Q4.
Gross margin was about 54% in Q2 versus about 70% last year. Management says this reflects the H1 mix: 30% retained and 70% paid to the accounting partner, with full-year margin expected at 65-70%.
Management believes AI will not remove agents: universities still need counsellors for visa and process support, and inter-university competition favours platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue gap came from post-August deferrals, and what gives confidence deferrals will convert rather than cancel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify deferrals by student count, since they span September, November and January intakes. It cited pipeline evidence (applications, deposits, visas) supporting 10-12% Q3 growth, and said many students have deferred to the January intake.

qa_highlights.question: Is the applications-to-revenue gap purely timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it was mainly students deferring, all timing-related, with no change in revenue per student.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 M&A or capital deployment be pursued given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is actively looking at M&A but is cautious given geopolitical uncertainty. Criteria include synergies, founders, source and destination jurisdictions, revenue and EBITDA; the target is EBITDA-accretive at 10-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone results hold up while consolidated results fell, and was the INR 57 crore termination fee one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone India books revenue on application processing, ahead of UK subsidiaries, which book on enrolment. The termination fee to Crizac Informatics UK (INR 57 crore vs INR 21.5 crore in FY25) was a one-time item that will not recur in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee cost and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is largely fixed and rose with acquisitions and tech hiring. Salary cost is expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term, and steady-state EBITDA margin is 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company diversify away from the UK, and when will non-UK revenue reach 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no date for 10% non-UK revenue. It expects 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30, citing New Zealand (via Medway), Netherlands, Europe and expected openings in Australia, Canada and the US.

risks_watch: Revenue is heavily concentrated: 44% of revenue came from three universities, and the UK is the dominant destination.
Q3 (+10-12% YoY) and FY27 (flat YoY) guidance depends on deferred students converting in Q3-Q4 and on the Q4 application pipeline. The company did not quantify the deferred student count.
US revenue is constrained by visa appointment limits; the Raj Consultants US presence has not scaled.
Cash conversion is above EBITDA (136% in H1) partly through working capital timing; management expects normalisation over the year.
Employee cost rising sharply as a share of revenue on acquisitions and tech hiring; EBITDA margin is seen at 25-26%.
The UK graduate-visa change depends on which universities qualify, and this is yet to be defined.
Buyback as a promoter tax-efficient route is blocked until the promoter holding falls below 75% (MPC compliance, about 3 years to achieve).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and on H2 recovery, but cautious on M&A and FY28, with no guidance given beyond FY27. Management was direct about the Q2 shortfall, framing it as timing. It was evasive on the deferred-student count and on the exact non-UK revenue timeline.
key_quotes: The revenue was therefore not lost.
Q2 was exceptional, driven by unforeseen external events.
EBITDA margin will be same as last year, 25% to 26%.
we expect Q3 FY '27 revenue to grow by 10 % to 12% over Q3 FY26 numbers

growth.why: FY27 revenue and profit guided flat, in line with FY26, with Q3 revenue guided +10-12% YoY backed by students already admitted with visas in place; Q2 revenue fell 36.7% on deferrals, and no capacity additions were disclosed (asset-light model).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides steady-state EBITDA margin at 25-26% (same as last year) while Q2 EBITDA margin was 32% and H1 30.6%, so the margin is guided to normalise down rather than expand; gross margin was ~54% in Q2 vs ~70% last year, with full-year gross margin guided at 65-70%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Asset-light model with no real estate acquisition planned; no new plants, lines or branches disclosed, only a Medway (NZ) acquisition that came live at the start of FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q3 FY27 revenue guided +10-12% YoY on students already admitted with visas in place, and Q2 applications fell only ~3% YoY while revenue fell ~37% on deferrals that management says will be recovered in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex not discussed beyond a USD 2.5 million commitment to in-house EduMentor AI platform (March 2026); no capacity-driven capex or utilisation figure given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue and profit guided only flat YoY in line with FY26, with Q2 revenue down 36.7% and H1 operating income down 18.3%, so an upgrade is not supported by the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 flat guidance depends on deferred students converting in Q3-Q4 and the Q4 pipeline, and the deferred count was not quantified; UK graduate-visa change from January 2027 is undefined.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: EduMentor AI matching and mentorship platform is in development with USD 2.5 million committed, but no launch date was given.

rows.label: Non-UK destination diversification to 30% of revenue by FY30
rows.why: Non-UK destinations were 9.5% of H1 applications vs 4.7% a year earlier but only 1.4% of revenue today, and no date was given for 10% non-UK revenue.

rows.label: Acquisitions with 10-20% return
rows.why: Management says the M&A pipeline is active but cautious, targeting EBITDA-accretive deals with 10-20% returns, against net cash of about INR 5,984 million.

rows.label: UK graduate visa change from January 2027
rows.why: The UK budget proposes a 2-year graduate visa for high-compliance universities vs 18 months for others, and three universities already account for 44% of revenue, but qualifying universities are yet to be defined.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 recovery and Q3 +10-12% growth, framing the Q2 shortfall as deferral timing, but was cautious on M&A, FY28 and the UK visa change, and evasive on the deferred-student count and the non-UK revenue timeline.
